answer: Under standard claim timelines, the main reimbursement claim must be submitted within 30 days from the date of discharge [2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [3]. An archived 2024 policy previously specified a deadline of 15 days from the date of discharge [1].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard retail plans, the Aurora Hospital Cash Benefit, and for declared conditions like hypertension, diabetes, and cardiac conditions unless explicitly waived [2][4][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan, the pre-existing disease waiting period is 24 months [2].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][2].

As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1]. However, this number is indicative because hospitals continuously join and leave the network, with the authoritative list maintained on the Aurora app and portal [1].

On the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured for each claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][4]. If a claim is made, the accumulated bonus is not reduced, but it stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment as infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are permanently excluded [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the initial outcome from customer service, you can escalate the dispute to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [1]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region, and you also retain the right to go to a consumer forum or civil court [3].
Ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation for road ambulance only, which is common to all plans [1][3][5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, and there is no separate waiting period [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [5]. It lasts for 15 days from receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. During this period, a policyholder can cancel and receive a premium refund minus proportionate risk premium, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [2]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [2].
For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][4].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].
